To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed the first technique for large scale, wafer-scale, high quality growth of atomically thin semiconducting transition metal dichalcgenides, which enables the batch fabrication of high mobility, wafer-scale monolayer transistors and other devices.

We have grown high quality, wafer scale monolayer Mo and W disulphide films with high electrical performance, and demonstrated their application in high performance transistions and vertically stacked devices.

we have developed a technique for the large scale, wafer scale, growth of high mobility semiconducting monolayers of MoS2 and WSe2 with high electrical performance and excellent spatial homogeneity on insulating Si/SiO2 substrates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the large-scale, high quality growth of atomically thin semiconducting transition metal dichalcogende films on insulating substraties.
the large-scale growth and electrical characterization of monolayer MoSe2 films.
the development of new materials for the large scale growth and integration of atomically thin semiconductors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the large scale, wafer scale, growth of semiconductive monolayers with high electrical performance has been achieved for the first time.
we have demonstrated the large scale growth and wafer scale homogenous of atomically thin TMD semiconductors with high electrical performance.

the authors have demonstrated the growth of high performance, wafer scale, three atom thick, monolayer Mo and W disulphide films, which can be used to produce high yield, wafer scale integrated circuits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that high mobility three atom thick monochalcogenide semiconducting layers can be grown with wafer scale uniformity, which is the key for the realization of atom thick integrated circuitry and other applications.

we have demonstrated the growth of high quality monolayer TDM films over a 4 inch area, which is the largest scale reported to date, with excellent spatial uniformity, and the batch fabrication of high mobility monolayer TMS transistors on a large scale.
we have developed the large scale, high performance growth of atomically thin semiconducting TMD films and their use in the batch fabrication of high yield, high performance transistores.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the large scale growth and high electrical performance of monolayer Mo S2 films can be achieved on a technologically important scale, and that the growth technique is applicable to other TMD materials.

the large scale, wafer scale growth of high quality monolayer semiconducting transition metal dichalcogens is now a reality, and this will open up new possibilities for atomically thin electronics, including the fabrication of high performance transistORS and photodetectorS with wafer scale integration, and the demonstration of new functionalities such as valleytronics.
it is now possible to produce wafer scale films, which is a prerequisite for large scale electronics applications.
